# Force-field engines

(engine-uff)=
## UFF

Universal Force Field (Rappe et al. 1992) -- covers the whole periodic table, native and in-process

Provides: charges, forces, periodic, stress, types

```{tabularcolumns} |\Y{0.18}|\Y{0.2}|\Y{0.18}|\Y{0.44}|
```

| Setting | Accepts | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Parameters** | one of UFF4MOF (UFF plus framework nodes), UFF (Rappe 1992 only) | `uff4mof` | UFF4MOF adds rows fitted to metal nodes in frameworks and types everything else exactly as UFF does.  Plain UFF never uses them, which is how to see what they change. |
| **Include electrostatics** | bool | `False` | Off by default, as in UFF itself: the published parameters were fitted without a Coulomb term. |
| **Charges from** | one of The sites, Equilibrate (QEq), Equilibrate (EQeq), All zero | `site` | Only used when electrostatics are on. |
| **van der Waals cutoff** | float, 4 to 30 A | `12.0` | The pair count goes as the cube of this: 10 A is 42% fewer pairs than 12 A, for an LJ tail worth about a thousandth of a kcal/mol per pair. |
| **Neighbour list skin** | float, 0 to 10 A | `2.0` | How far an atom may move before the pair list is rebuilt. |

(engine-xtb)=
## xTB (GFN)

Semiempirical tight binding and the GFN force field, through the tblite or xtb binary -- no parameter set to download and no atom typing to get right.

Provides: forces, periodic

```{tabularcolumns} |\Y{0.18}|\Y{0.2}|\Y{0.18}|\Y{0.44}|
```

| Setting | Accepts | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Method** | one of GFN2-xTB, GFN1-xTB, GFN-FF | `gfn2` | GFN2-xTB is the default and the most accurate of the three; GFN1-xTB is older and more robust for metals; GFN-FF is a force field and is orders of magnitude faster, which for a framework of a few thousand atoms is the difference between a relaxation and an afternoon.  The method decides which binary runs: tblite for the two tight-binding ones and xtb for GFN-FF. |
| **Total charge** | float, -20 to 20 e | `0.0` |  |
| **Accuracy** | float, 0.01 to 1000 | `1.0` | The SCF convergence criterion, as a multiplier: smaller is tighter and slower.  Ignored by GFN-FF, which has no SCF. |
| **Electronic temperature** | float, 0 to 10000 K | `300.0` | Fermi filling.  Not zero by default, for the same reason DFTB+'s is not: a metallic framework at exactly zero has no gap to fill and the cycle oscillates rather than failing. |
| **Max SCF iterations** | int, 1 to 10000 | `250` |  |

(engine-mace)=
## MACE (machine-learned)

A machine-learned potential in the atomic cluster expansion family.  The MACE-MP foundation models answer for a framework with no parameters to assign and no atom typing to get right, at a cost between a force field's and tight binding's.

Provides: forces, periodic, stress

```{tabularcolumns} |\Y{0.18}|\Y{0.2}|\Y{0.18}|\Y{0.44}|
```

| Setting | Accepts | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Model** | one of MACE-MPA-0 -- MPtrj + sAlex, PBE+U (recommended), MACE-MP-0b3 -- MPtrj, PBE+U, steadier under pressure, MACE-OMAT-0 -- OMat, PBE+U [ASL licence], MACE-MATPES-r2SCAN-0 -- r2SCAN, no +U [ASL licence], MACE-MH-1 -- crystals, molecules and surfaces [ASL licence], MACE-MP-MOF0 -- 127 MOFs, PBE-D3(BJ), for phonons; 26 elements [CC BY 4.0, cite], MACE-MP-0a medium -- the default before mace 0.3.10, MACE-MP-0a small -- fastest, MACE-MP-0a large, A model file of my own | `medium-mpa-0` | The MACE-MP foundation models are fitted over the Materials Project and need nothing assigning -- they answer for a framework whose metal node UFF has no parameters for.  Each is downloaded once, to MACE's own cache.  Choose 'a model file of my own' for one you have fitted. |
| **Model file** | path |  | A .model file, for the 'my own' choice above.  Ignored by the MACE-MP models. |
| **Run on** | one of Whatever is fastest here, CPU, Apple GPU (mps), NVIDIA GPU (cuda) | `auto` | A GPU is worth an order of magnitude on a framework of a few thousand atoms.  'Whatever is fastest here' asks torch what this machine has. |
| **Double precision** | bool | `True` | Leave this on for geometry optimisation: in single precision the model's own noise is larger than the energy differences an optimiser is reading, and the line search wanders instead of converging. |

(engine-orb)=
## ORB-v3 (machine-learned)

Orbital Materials' universal potential.  Like MACE it needs no parameters assigning.  Run here without a dispersion correction, so a relaxed framework's volume differs by a percent or more from the benchmark that ranks it among the most accurate, which added D3.

Provides: forces, periodic, stress

```{tabularcolumns} |\Y{0.18}|\Y{0.2}|\Y{0.18}|\Y{0.44}|
```

| Setting | Accepts | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Model** | one of ORB-v3 -- OMat24, all neighbours within 6 A (recommended), ORB-v3 -- OMat24, 20 neighbours, faster, ORB-v3 -- MPtrj + Alexandria, all neighbours within 6 A, ORB-v3 -- MPtrj + Alexandria, 20 neighbours, faster | orb-v3-conservative-inf-omat | Conservative ORB-v3 models only: their forces are the gradient of their energy, which is what a relaxation needs.  Each is downloaded once, to orb-models' own cache. |
| **Run on** | one of The NVIDIA GPU if there is one, otherwise the CPU, CPU, NVIDIA GPU (cuda) | `auto` | orb-models cannot run on an Apple GPU, so on a Mac this is the CPU. |
| **Double precision** | bool | `True` | Leave this on for geometry optimisation: in single precision the model's own noise is a third of the energy differences an optimiser reads.  Off is about 2.7 times faster. |

(engine-mattersim)=
## MatterSim (machine-learned)

Microsoft's universal potential, an M3GNet trained across temperature and pressure.  Like MACE it needs no parameters assigning, and it is the fastest of the three.  Its authors note relatively low accuracy for organic polymeric systems, which is the linker half of a framework; run here without a dispersion correction.

Provides: forces, periodic, stress

```{tabularcolumns} |\Y{0.18}|\Y{0.2}|\Y{0.18}|\Y{0.44}|
```

| Setting | Accepts | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Model** | one of MatterSim 1M -- the smaller model, faster (recommended), MatterSim 5M -- five times the parameters, more accurate | MatterSim-v1.0.0-1M | Each is downloaded once, to ~/.local/mattersim. |
| **Run on** | one of The NVIDIA GPU if there is one, otherwise the CPU, CPU, NVIDIA GPU (cuda) | `auto` | MatterSim cannot load onto an Apple GPU, so on a Mac this is the CPU. |
| **Double precision** | bool | `True` | Leave this on for geometry optimisation: in single precision the model's own noise is a noticeable part of the energy differences an optimiser reads.  Off is about 1.5 times faster. |

(engine-dftb)=
## DFTB+

Density-functional tight binding, through the DFTB+ binary -- DFT-like and fast enough to relax a framework UFF can only approximate.

Provides: forces, periodic

```{tabularcolumns} |\Y{0.18}|\Y{0.2}|\Y{0.18}|\Y{0.44}|
```

| Setting | Accepts | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hamiltonian** | one of DFTB3 (third order, needs 3ob), SCC-DFTB (self-consistent charges), Non-SCC DFTB (fastest, no charge transfer) | `dftb3` | The nearest thing DFTB has to a functional.  DFTB3 is third order and is what the 3ob set was fitted for; SCC-DFTB is second order and works with any set; non-SCC has no charge transfer at all and is for a first look. |
| **Parameter directory** | path |  | The folder of Slater-Koster .skf files.  They are separate downloads from dftb.org -- 3ob for organics, matsci for inorganic solids.  Left empty, the DFTB_PREFIX environment variable is used. |
| **Dispersion** | one of None, DFT-D3 with Becke-Johnson damping, Lennard-Jones (universal force field radii) | `none` | DFTB has no dispersion of its own, and a framework's pore size is a dispersion-bound number -- so for a porous solid this is not an optional refinement. |
| **Total charge** | float, -20 to 20 e | `0.0` |  |
| **Electronic temperature** | float, 0 to 10000 K | `300.0` | Fermi filling.  Not zero by default: a metallic framework at exactly zero has no gap to fill and the SCC cycle oscillates for ever rather than failing. |
| **K-point spacing** | float, 0 to 2 1/A | `0.25` | The mesh is worked out from the cell: a cell twice as long gets half as many k-points along it.  Zero is the Gamma point alone, which is what a large cell wants. |
| **SCC tolerance** | float, 1e-09 to 0.01 | `1e-05` |  |
| **Max SCC iterations** | int, 1 to 10000 | `250` |  |
| **Angular momentum overrides** | text |  | Per element, as 'Cl=d, Zn=d'.  The built-in table follows 3ob; a set that disagrees with it gives a number rather than an error, which is why this is here. |
